I picked up The First Descendant on launch week and it didn't grab me back then. For some reason, I decided to check it out later. I really deeply enjoyed it for a few weeks in a row after that, a lot seemed to have been improved, specifically the new player experience. 

Well, I decided after playing nearly eighty hours It was worth it for me to give in and get ONE VERY SPECIFIC pay-to-wear cosmetic that was advertised on a sale. It was in fact the in-game reflected sale price of this item that finally convinced me, a free player to buy clown money. I purchased my The First Descendant clown money and tried to buy my item. But the transaction failed. Did nothing. Over and over again, nothing. I contacted customer support and I did everything they suggested, with no change.

When I responded, they told me to wait for the next patch. So, waited. The next patch came about two weeks later, and removed the sale of the item I wanted. To be clear, the item is still available, for a much higher, non-sale price. That was their solution. I know I was able to buy other items, because I ended up successfully wasting money a lesser-wanted cosmetic just to see if there was something wrong with my account entirely. Nope. 

So at least for me, false advertisement left a bad feeling... But I should have known better. I've spent less on entire games with better ethics, than I did on a cosmetic that they wouldn't even let me buy. 

See you some other time, ladies. had fun.

Honestly, I went into The First Descendant expecting just another generic looter shooter… and while it definitely sticks to that formula, it’s still really fun if that’s your kind of game

The gunplay feels smooth, abilities look great, and the overall sci fi style is super polished. The Descendants themselves are a BIG highlight, with some of them being super lovable (looking at you Bunny), both in their design and personality! A few actually stand out enough that I found myself sticking with them not just for their abilities, but because I genuinely feel in love with them

IT’s got that easy “zone out and grind” kind of gameplay loop, which can be relaxing in the right mood. But yeah, it does start to feel repetitive after a while. Missions blur together, and the grind can get pretty heavy if you’re trying to progress without spending anything. The usual FtP systems are definitely here, so expect some farming or waiting

The First Descendant has some flaws but has a ton of potential thanks to its strong core gameplay, slick visuals, and a cast of characters that are easy to get attached to. The foundation is definitely there for something great, it just needs more variety, better mission design, and a more balanced grind to really shine. If the developers keep updating it and listening to feedback, it could easily grow into one of the better looter shooters out there

Overall: Smooth gameplay, great visuals, lovable characters, and is super fun but gets grindy and repetitive after some time so dont expect your time to be respected 

Easy 8.5/10 for me highly recommend giving this a playthrough
